name: Content Repurposer with Brand Voice and Channel Rules

parameters.content:
## Content Repurposer with Brand Voice and Channel Rules

One long article becomes a set of channel ready drafts that already follow your
brand voice and each platform's character limits. It works two ways: as a POST
endpoint your own tools can call, and as a daily job that picks up new posts
from your blog feed on its own.

### How it works

An API request is checked for sixty words and answered with a 400 when it is
too thin, so no model is paid for scraps. The scheduled path reads your feed,
keeps only posts from the last day, strips the HTML and caps the batch at three
articles. Both paths meet in one brief builder that trims long pieces at a
sentence boundary. A brand voice row is then read from a sheet, giving the
writer the brand name, audience, tone, call to action, preferred hashtags and
banned words, so drafts sound like you rather than like a model. The agent
returns structured JSON: a summary, key points, three alternative hooks, a
thread, a LinkedIn post, an Instagram caption, a newsletter blurb and hashtags.
Character limits are then enforced in code rather than trusted to the model.
Over-length posts are split or trimmed, hashtags deduplicated and capped,
banned words removed, and every fix recorded. Each draft lands in a queue tab
as its own row marked Needs review, so a human approves before publishing. API
callers get the set back as JSON, scheduled runs post a Slack summary.

### Setup

Connect Sheets, Slack and your model credentials. Fill one Brand Voice row and
create the Content Queue tab with the columns named on those nodes. Set your
feed URL and Slack channel.

### Customization

Change the channel limits or add a channel in the fan-out step.

## Call it from your own tools
A POST request with a content field. Anything under sixty words is rejected with a 400 before a model is called.

## Or let it watch your blog
Each morning the feed is read, posts older than a day are dropped, the HTML is stripped and the batch is capped so one busy day cannot run up a bill.

## One brief, your brand voice
Both entry points meet here. Long pieces are trimmed at a sentence boundary, then the brand voice row is attached to every brief.

## Write the drafts
The agent returns structured JSON for every channel at once. Gemini stands in if the main model fails.

## Enforce the rules, then queue
Character limits, hashtag caps and banned words are applied in code, not trusted to the model. Each draft lands in the queue tab as its own row marked Needs review.

## Answer or announce
The run collapses to one item. API callers get every draft back as JSON, scheduled runs post a summary to Slack.

options.systemMessage:
You turn one long piece of content into ready to post drafts for several channels.

Voice
- Write as the brand you are given, for the audience you are given, in the tone you are given.
- Never use the banned words listed in the brief.
- Never invent statistics, quotes, prices, dates or customer names. Use only what the source text says.
- Do not use emoji, exclamation marks or phrases like game changer, unlock, supercharge or dive in.

Per channel
- summary: two or three sentences a busy reader can skim.
- keyPoints: four to six short takeaways, each a full sentence.
- hookVariants: three different opening lines for the same idea, so a human can pick one.
- tweetThread: four to seven posts. Each one must be under 270 characters and must make sense on its own.
- linkedinPost: one post of roughly 120 to 200 words, first person, ending in the call to action from the brief.
- instagramCaption: under 150 words, plain sentences, no hashtags in the text itself.
- newsletterBlurb: a short paragraph that teases the piece and links out.
- hashtags: three to five topical tags without the hash symbol.

Return only the requested JSON fields.
